Description: As a user, I want to create a habit by providing a name, category, target frequency, and optional description, so that I can start tracking my habits.
As a user, I want to edit an existing habit's name, category, target frequency, and description, so that I can update my habit details.
As a user, I want to delete an existing habit, so that I can remove habits I no longer want to track.
As a user, I want to prevent creating two habits with the same name, so that I can avoid confusion and duplication.

Summary: Ensure habit names are not empty
Description: As a user, I want habit names to be non-empty, so that I can create meaningful habits.
As a user, I want to mark a habit as completed for the current day, so that I can track my progress.
As a user, I want to undo today's completion if it was recorded by mistake, so that I can correct my tracking.
As a user, I want the application to automatically record the completion date, so that I don't have to manually enter it.
As a user, I want the application to calculate my current streak, so that I can see how many consecutive days I have completed a habit.
As a user, I want the application to calculate my longest streak, so that I can see the highest number of consecutive days I have completed a habit.
As a user, I want the application to calculate the total number of times I have completed a habit, so that I can see my overall progress.
As a user, I want the application to calculate my completion rate, so that I can see the percentage of days I have completed a habit.
As a user, I want the dashboard to display the total number of active habits, so that I can see how many habits I am currently tracking.
As a user, I want the dashboard to display the number of habits I completed today, so that I can see my progress for the day.
As a user, I want the dashboard to display the number of habits I missed today, so that I can see areas for improvement.
As a user, I want the dashboard to display my best current streak, so that I can see the highest streak I have achieved.
As a user, I want the statistics to update immediately after any change, so that I can see the most current data.

Summary: View calendar showing completed and missed days
Description: As a user, I want to view a calendar showing completed and missed days for each habit, so that I can see my progress over time.
As a user, I want past records to remain available even after editing a habit's description or category, so that I can review my history.
As a user, I want to restrict editing of completion records older than seven days, so that I can maintain accurate historical data.
As a user, I want to configure a daily reminder time, so that I don't forget to complete my habits.
As a user, I want to receive a notification for my daily reminder, so that I am reminded to complete my habits.
As a user, I want to disable notifications if I don't want to be reminded, so that I can focus on my habits without interruptions.
As a user, I want the reminder time change to apply immediately, so that I can adjust my schedule accordingly.
As a user, I want all data to be stored locally, so that it remains available after restarting the application.
As a user, I want the application to recover previously saved data automatically when launched, so that I don't lose my progress.
As a user, I want the application to handle failed operations without leaving the data in an inconsistent state, so that I can continue using the application.

Summary: Include separate sections for Dashboard, Habits, Calendar, Statistics, and Settings
Description: As a user, I want the application to include separate sections for Dashboard, Habits, Calendar, Statistics, and Settings, so that I can easily access different features.

Summary: Display confirmation messages for successful operations
Description: As a user, I want confirmation messages to be displayed for successful operations, so that I know my actions have been completed.
As a user, I want validation errors to be clearly explained, so that I understand what went wrong and how to fix it.
